web_title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix
book_title: Prologue: Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict, and the Opportunity Matrix
question: Why does Macpower CNC earn a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL business quality rating yet receive a strict REJECTED (TIER_0) verdict at ₹2,080?

epigraph.quote: Great underwriting separates two questions: is this a machine-tool franchise worth owning, and is today's price offering you an asymmetric bet?
epigraph.author: Dossier Opening Thesis

web_blocks.html: Macpower CNC Machines Limited (NSE: MACPOWER) is a strong domestic manufacturing story. However, its stock price has outgrown its current fundamentals [1, 23]. Over twenty-three years in Rajkot, Gujarat, founder Rupesh Mehta and his team built a ₹333 Cr (FY26) precision CNC platform from a ₹64 Cr assembly shop [1, 2, 15]. Today, the business delivers 29% ROCE, 16.18% operating margins, and ₹25.62 Cr in net cash as of Sep-2026 [1, 4, 15]. Its order book also hit a record ₹476.7 Cr, up 36% YoY, with 40% coming from premium NEXA machines [4, 15]. Q2 FY27 revenue surged 40.4% YoY to ₹120.33 Cr, while H1 FY27 operating cash flow rebounded to ₹29.97 Cr [4, 15]. These results prove that Macpower's backward integration and product-mix upgrades are real [4, 15].

Our two-stage underwriting separates price-blind business quality (Chapters 1–6) from live valuation and tape structure (Chapters 7–9). That discipline yields a clear, unhedged verdict: REJECTED (TIER_0) for new capital at ₹2,080.00, driven by VALUATION and CASH_FLOW [1, 23]. On a price-blind basis, Macpower earns CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL and PASS_WITH_WATCH. Roughly 90% of its non-material cost base is fixed, which creates sharp operating deleverage during MSME downturns [1, 17]. Inventory sits at 259 days (a 182-day cash conversion cycle), and the 2,500-machine plant is capped near 95% utilization until a 13-acre facility opens in Q2 FY28 [1, 15]. At ₹2,080, the stock trades at 48.40x TTM P/E, 10.57x P/B, and over 600x FY26 FCF [1, 23]. Reverse DCF implies ~22–24% annual revenue growth for seven years with zero cyclical dips [1, 23]. The chart sits in a constructive Stage 2 pullback near its 50D SMA (₹2,050.27) [24]. Even so, our ₹2,280 Base Target (+9.6%) versus ₹1,548–₹1,675 structural risk (-19.5% to -25.6%) offers only ~0.49:1 asymmetry. That falls well short of our 1.50:1 hurdle [23, 24].

web_blocks.html: We organize this monograph in two strictly isolated passes. Chapters 1 through 6 evaluate Macpower on a price-blind basis. They trace its 2003 Rajkot origin, 388+ machine portfolio, 259-day inventory cycle, and 13-acre expansion plan to set our CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality rating. Chapters 7 through 9 remove those blinders to test valuation via Reverse DCF and peer multiples. They also inspect the 1W/1D/4H Stage 2 chart and NSE F&O absence. Finally, they deliver an unhedged REJECTED (TIER_0) action plan with a ₹1,550–₹1,680 watchlist trigger.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our institutional deep dive on Macpower CNC Machines Limited. Before we walk through twenty-three years of shop-floor history in Rajkot, I want to give you our bottom-line conclusion up front—and explain why a genuinely impressive Indian manufacturing business can still be a disciplined pass at today's market price.

If you judge Macpower purely on its business execution, there is much to admire. Founded in 2003 by Rupesh Mehta, the company has systematically climbed the precision-engineering ladder: from basic Turner lathes at 2.5% operating margins before its 2018 IPO, to a backward-integrated 2,500-machine platform earning 16% operating margins, 29% return on capital employed, and ₹25.6 crore in net cash. In Q2 FY27, sales hit an all-time quarterly record of ₹120.33 crore, operating cash flow rebounded to ₹29.97 crore in the first half, and the order book reached ₹476.7 crore—with 40% in higher-value NEXA machines.

Yet when you and I remove our price blinders in Chapters 7 through 9, the investment math breaks down. At ₹2,080 per share, Macpower trades at 48.4 times trailing earnings, 10.57 times book value, and over 600 times FY26 free cash flow. Our Reverse DCF shows that the market is already pricing in 22% to 24% annual revenue growth for the next seven years with zero cyclical downturns—ignoring the reality that Macpower's sales fell 42% in FY20, its inventory sits at 259 days, and its existing plant is already running at 95% capacity until a new 13-acre unit arrives in FY28.

Even though the stock is in a Stage 2 uptrend near its 50-day moving average of ₹2,050, our Base Case target of ₹2,280 offers just 9.6% upside against 20% to 26% structural downside risk to ₹1,548–₹1,675. That 0.49-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio fails our 1.50-to-1 hurdle. Our verdict at ₹2,080 is REJECTED, Tier 0. Because Macpower is not held in our portfolio, we take zero action today, keep 100% of marginal cash in reserve, and set a patient price alert for ₹1,550 to ₹1,680.

How should you use this monograph as you listen or read through the nine chapters ahead? Notice that we built this dossier in two strictly separated stages—a discipline designed to protect you from narrative bias. In Chapters 1 through 6, we lock the ticker price in a drawer. We examine Macpower's shop floor in Metoda GIDC, its 2018 IPO backward integration, its 64% Turning Center and 35% VMC product mix, its NEXA premiumization push, its 259-day inventory cycle, and its 29% return on capital employed without ever mentioning whether the stock is cheap or expensive.

Only after we have earned an honest, price-blind judgment on the business—calling it Cyclical Conditional with a Pass-With-Watch on KPI health—do we open the market quote in Chapter 7. There, we run a Reverse DCF to uncover the 22% to 24% seven-year growth rate baked into ₹2,080, compare Macpower against Jyoti CNC, LMW, Kennametal India, and Wendt India, and test the Stage 2 chart in Chapter 8.

That two-stage discipline is what keeps you from falling in love with a great factory at a dangerous price. Enjoy the deep dive into one of Gujarat's finest machine-tool builders—and remember why patience at ₹2,080 is our highest-conviction edge.

To make this decision immediately actionable for you, let us summarize the exact numbers you need to remember. Macpower closed at ₹2,080.00 on November 20, 2026, with a market cap of ₹2,080.87 crore. Our probability-weighted expected value across Bull (25% at ₹2,850), Base (50% at ₹2,280), and Bear (25% at ₹1,450) scenarios is ₹2,215.00—just +6.5% above the current price, against a -30.3% Bear Case drawdown.

Because we already hold zero shares of Macpower in our portfolio, we have no position to trim or defend. Our holding action is NOT_HELD, our new-capital verdict is REJECTED (Tier 0), and our next marginal ₹1,00,000 unit stays 100% in cash. Keep your eye on the ₹1,550 to ₹1,680 margin-of-safety zone—because in cyclical capital goods, patience is the highest-returning skill you own.

As you move into Chapter 1, keep both scorecards in mind: admire the twenty-three-year Rajkot engineering build, respect the 29% ROCE and ₹476.7 crore order book, and never forget that at ₹2,080, discipline means keeping your powder dry until price or cash conversion shifts decisively in your favor.

Every number in this dossier—from the ₹333.18 crore audited FY26 revenue and ₹476.7 crore September 2026 order book to the ₹2,080.00 session close, ₹2,050.27 50-day moving average, and ₹2,215.00 probability-weighted expected value—is traced directly to primary filings and verified market snapshots as of November 20, 2026.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Our job as disciplined investors is not to admire good companies at any price; it is to demand asymmetric odds. At ₹2,080, Macpower is priced for perfection. At ₹1,550–₹1,680, it becomes a conversation.
